**Probably yes, but it is not yet confirmed under the analysis rules.**

- Hansen data show 13.5 ha of tree-cover loss in 2025, about 3.9% of the 345.6 ha asset.
- The JRC 2020 map shows 98% of that area was forest in 2020.
- The MGAP 2021 forest map classes 13.1 ha as native forest, 0.4 ha as outside mapped forest, and none as planted forest.

The corroboration rule requires a later year of data showing the loss persisted. 2025 is the latest year observed, so that check could not be run. The loss is therefore flagged but not corroborated.

Also, the data show tree-cover loss, not its cause. Fire, storm damage, or clearing that later regrows would look the same, and the data do not show what the land became afterward. Rechecking once 2026 data are available would settle it.
